drivers.lead: Johnson's five consecutive titles, 2006 to 2010, are the longest run in Cup Series history
drivers.note: One thing needs saying before the rest, because this page counts from 2000, which is where our NASCAR records begin. Within that window Jimmie Johnson stands alone on seven. All-time he does not: Richard Petty won seven between 1964 and 1979 and Dale Earnhardt seven between 1980 and 1994, so the Cup Series record is a three-way tie rather than his alone. What is his alone is the run of five. Those came under the ten-race Chase format, his sixth in 2013 under the same rules, and his seventh in 2016 under the elimination playoff that replaced it — so he won titles under two systems designed, in part, to stop exactly that kind of dominance. He last contested a full Cup season in 2020. Joey Logano is the closest active driver on three, from 2018, 2022 and 2024.
